lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Guided practice: giving and receiving feedback

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic giving and receiving feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner picks one real shared activity or task with someone in the household this week, such as a chore, a game, or a project done together, gives feedback on it using the what-worked/what-to-try structure, and asks for feedback in return about their own contribution.

simulationAlternative.description: If no shared activity happens with a household member this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined exchange: a specific shared task, the what-worked/what-to-try feedback the learner would give about it, and the feedback the learner imagines receiving in return, including how they would respond to hearing it.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain which was harder for you, giving the feedback or receiving it, and describe one specific change you would make to how you deliver feedback next time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently. | Two-way exchange: The learner reports both the feedback they gave and the feedback they received, each with specific detail. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner repeat the exchange with a different household member on a different shared task and compare how the two people responded to receiving the same feedback structure.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic giving and receiving feedback task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner picks one real shared activity or task with someone in the household this week, such as a chore, a game, or a project done together, gives feedback on it using the what-worked/what-to-try structure, and asks for feedback in return about their own contribution.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact giving and receiving feedback decision or action.
Model move 2: Recall a recent time someone gave you feedback, or you gave someone feedback, that did not land well.
Model move 3: Practice the two-part feedback structure: one specific thing that worked, and one specific thing to try differently next time.

Model check: Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently. | Two-way exchange: The learner reports both the feedback they gave and the feedback they received, each with specific detail.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for giving and receiving feedback.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner picks one real shared activity or task with someone in the household this week, such as a chore, a game, or a project done together, gives feedback on it using the what-worked/what-to-try structure, and asks for feedback in return about their own contribution.
Coach direction: Recall a recent time someone gave you feedback, or you gave someone feedback, that did not land well.
Learner prompt: Describe what was said and why it didn't land well (too vague, felt like criticism, no specific detail, or something else).
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Practice the two-part feedback structure: one specific thing that worked, and one specific thing to try differently next time.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My practice feedback names one specific thing that worked, not a general compliment.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My practice feedback names one specific, doable thing to try differently, not a criticism of the person.

Equal-access rule: If no shared activity happens with a household member this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined exchange: a specific shared task, the what-worked/what-to-try feedback the learner would give about it, and the feedback the learner imagines receiving in return, including how they would respond to hearing it.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain which was harder for you, giving the feedback or receiving it, and describe one specific change you would make to how you deliver feedback next time.

Success checks: Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently. | Two-way exchange: The learner reports both the feedback they gave and the feedback they received, each with specific detail.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: giving and receiving feedback supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional giving and receiving feedback condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently. | Two-way exchange: The learner reports both the feedback they gave and the feedback they received, each with specific detail..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner picks one real shared activity or task with someone in the household this week, such as a chore, a game, or a project done together, gives feedback on it using the what-worked/what-to-try structure, and asks for feedback in return about their own contribution.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Describe what was said and why it didn't land well (too vague, felt like criticism, no specific detail, or something else).
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.
guidedFirstAttempt.successCondition: Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently.
guidedFirstAttempt.correctionTurn: Use the fresh condition on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-guided-card: change one constraint, redo only the affected move, and state why the corrected move now meets the success check.

realRoute.title: giving and receiving feedback — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Practice the two-part feedback structure: one specific thing that worked, and one specific thing to try differently next time.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: giving and receiving feedback — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If no shared activity happens with a household member this week, the learner instead writes a short imagined exchange: a specific shared task, the what-worked/what-to-try feedback the learner would give about it, and the feedback the learner imagines receiving in return, including how they would respond to hearing it.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain which was harder for you, giving the feedback or receiving it, and describe one specific change you would make to how you deliver feedback next time.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Feedback specificity: The feedback names one specific thing that worked and one specific thing to try differently. | Two-way exchange: The learner reports both the feedback they gave and the feedback they received, each with specific detail.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l03-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
